metadata.title: Darren Waller a Boom/Bust TE Option if Active
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers veteran tight end Darren Waller (knee) disappointed in Week 10 in a good-on-paper matchup against the Saints after posting eight catches for 90 yards and a touchdown just a week prior. Waller went for 24 yards on two catches and four targets in Week 11 and now enters this week with a questionable designation, getting in two limited practices due to a knee injury. Head coach Dave Canales, however, is "very hopeful" that Waller will play, along with teammate Tommy Tremble (knee). Waller has 11.5 half-PPR points or more in three of nine games this season, and has scored his four touchdowns in those games. The Panthers' Week 11 opponent, the Baltimore Ravens, have allowed middle-of-the-league fantasy points to the tight end position, but rank in the top eight most TDs allowed to them. Waller has been at his most involved all season over the past three games, averaging a 59% snap share. Assuming Waller suits up, he will remain a high-end TE2 with strong upside, but quite a low floor. In a seemingly desolate Week 11 TE landscape, Darren Waller is an acceptable start for fantasy managers who don't have a locked-in top option.

metadata.title: Darren Waller (knee) listed questionable Sunday
metadata.description: Darren Waller is listed as questionable for Sunday's game against the Ravens.
metadata.analysis: Waller got in limited practices on Thursday and Friday. He should be trending towards being good to go for Sunday. He remains a TE2 for fantasy managers with Tommy Tremble also expected to play.

Waller's production has been all over the place this season, making him difficult to pin down as a reliable weekly fantasy option. He's more of a best-ball type of fantasy asset.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Questionable for Sunday, "Hopeful" to Play
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller (knee) is questionable to play on Sunday in the Week 11 contest against the visiting Baltimore Ravens, according to The Athletic's Joe Person. With that said, head coach Dave Canales said he is "very hopeful" that Waller and fellow TE Tommy Tremble (knee) will play this weekend after a couple of days of good work in practice. The 34-year-old Waller has been hit-and-miss this season in his first year in Carolina, with his last two games a perfect example of the volatility he gives fantasy managers willing to try him as a TE2 streamer. In the Week 9 loss to the Denver Broncos, Waller exploded for eight catches on 10 targets for a season-high 90 yards and his fourth touchdown of the season. But in last week's win over the division-rival New Orleans Saints, he caught just two passes for 24 yards on four targets. He will have a revenge game against the Ravens this weekend if he plays, but Waller will be a boom/bust, touchdown-dependent TE2 option in a Panthers passing attack that has gone stale in recent weeks after a strong start in 2026. RotoBaller has the veteran tight end ranked No. 16 at his position in Week 11 in half-PPR scoring.

metadata.analysis: One day removed from being a non-participant Wednesday due to a knee injury, Waller was able to mix into some drills, but he now has just one more chance to get back to full Friday, at which point his odds to suit up Sunday against the Ravens will become known.

metadata.title: Darren Waller - Practicing Thursday

metadata.title: Darren Waller Returns to Practice on a Limited Basis
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller (knee) was limited Thursday, according to The Charlotte Observer's Mike Kaye, after being listed as a non-participant on Wednesday's estimated report. Waller has drawn 14 targets over his past two games, with 10 coming against the Denver Broncos in Week 9. He finished that game with a season-high eight catches for 90 yards and a touchdown. In the Week 10 win over the New Orleans Saints, he played 43 of 70 offensive snaps and caught two of four targets for 24 yards. Carolina opened that game with Waller and Tommy Tremble on the field together, and Mitchell Evans played half the offensive snaps. Tremble (knee) also returned to limited work Thursday ahead of Sunday's game against the Baltimore Ravens. Waller's 25 catches are tied with Tremble for the most among Carolina's tight ends, and his four touchdown catches lead the team. He's had more than three catches in only two of his nine games, with three of his four scores coming on a combined four catches against Atlanta and Tampa Bay.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Misses Practice on Wednesday with Knee Injury

The severity of Waller's knee issue is unclear, but it appears his availability for Carolina's Week 11 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens could be in question. Across nine games in 2026, the 34-year-old has recorded 25 catches for 323 yards and four touchdowns on 39 targets. Waller logged a season-high eight catches for 90 yards and a touchdown in Week 9 against the Denver Broncos, but he followed that up with just a two-catch performance against the New Orleans Saints in Week 10. Panthers tight end Tommy Tremble (knee) also missed practice on Wednesday, so the team could be very shorthanded at the position on Sunday.

metadata.title: Darren Waller has Waiver Appeal as Big-Play TE2 Streamer
metadata.description: It is almost impossible to predict when Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller's big games will come, especially as he works in a tight end committee in Carolina. The 34-year-old veteran blew up for his best game of the season in the Week 9 loss to the Denver Broncos, catching eight of his 10 targets for 90 yards and his fourth touchdown of the year, but he followed it up with another quiet performance in Sunday's 20-17 win over the division-rival New Orleans Saints by catching two of his four targets for just 24 yards. The former Pro Bowler does have a decent 12.9-yard-per-catch average through nine games in his first year in Carolina, and he remains a strong red-zone target for quarterback Bryce Young. Fantasy managers will always be running the risk that Waller will produce a dud if they throw him into their lineup, but he will have some waiver-wire appeal going into a Week 11 matchup with the fading Baltimore Ravens this week. Going into the Ravens' Monday night matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 10, they ranked as the 12th-best matchup for tight ends in terms of half-PPR points allowed per game in 2026, and it will be a revenge game for Waller against the organization that drafted him in the sixth round in 2015 out of Georgia Tech. With bye weeks still in effect in Week 11, there will be plenty of TE2 options with much less upside.

metadata.title: Darren Waller - Two catches in Week 10
metadata.description: Waller caught two of four targets for 24 yards in Sunday's 20-17 win over the Saints.
metadata.analysis: One week after his 8-90-1 receiving outburst, Waller came back to normalcy in the Panthers' three-man committee at tight end. Waller has big upside, but his ceiling games are difficult to predict. He's been held below 40 yards with no touchdowns in five of nine games this season. Waller will be a low-floor TE2 with upside for Week 11 against the Ravens.

metadata.title: Darren Waller hauls in two passes in Week 10
metadata.description: Darren Waller caught 2-of-4 targets for 24 yards in a 20-17 win over the Saints.
metadata.analysis: Waller's performance was a massive drop-off from his 8-90-1 line from last week. It will be tough to trust the veteran in Week 11 against Baltimore.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Is Tough to Start in Week 10
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller put together a fantastic performance as the overall TE1 in Week 9 against the Broncos, catching eight passes for 90 yards and a touchdown on 10 targets, the most targets he has drawn in a game since 2023. The three weeks prior to Week 9, Waller had only been targeted two times a game, so it is tough to project Waller to continue with such great involvement. However, the Panthers' Week 10 opponent, the New Orleans Saints, have allowed 16.4 fantasy points per game (seventh in the league) and five touchdowns in eight games to opposing tight ends. Waller has the opportunity to take advantage, similar to Week 9, of a soft defense matchup for tight ends. While it is not likely that Waller receives as many targets, he projects as a TE2, with upside for more if he can get into the end zone, as he has already done four times this year. Fantasy managers in tight end premium leagues can consider Waller in Week 10, but in standard leagues, Waller should probably remain on the bench unless in a pinch, as RotoBaller's TE20.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Turning Heads After 10-Target Performance
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller has been inconsistent week over week this season, but his performance this past Sunday against the Denver Broncos could be enough to justify adding him off waivers in most leagues. Waller exploded for eight catches on 10 targets Sunday, adding 90 yards and one touchdown along the way. Carolina found itself playing behind and relying on passing attempts -- often to Waller and Tetairoa McMillan -- to keep them in the game. The veteran's inconsistency this year does prevent him from having immediate TE1 status in fantasy football, but he's absolutely trending in the right direction. Plus, Carolina has tough matchups coming up against the Saints, Ravens, Buccaneers, and Vikings, creating some potential negative game script environments in which the Panthers could look to throw the ball early and often. Managers should consider adding Waller off waivers, especially in deeper leagues or scenarios where managers may need a quick bye week fill-in.

metadata.title: Darren Waller totals 90 yards and touchdown in Week 9
metadata.description: Darren Waller caught eight of 10 targets for 90 yards and one touchdown in the Panthers' 26-21 loss to the Broncos in Week 9.
metadata.analysis: Waller scored from 15 yards out in the third quarter to give Carolina a 14-13 lead. He also led the Panthers in receptions, targets, and receiving yards. That's a significant improvement from his one-catch, 11-yard performance in Week 8. Waller was Bryce Young's primary receiving option Sunday and has the production to warrant consideration as a fantasy starter against the Saints in Week 10.

metadata.title: Darren Waller - Leading receiver in Week 9 loss
metadata.description: Waller caught eight of 10 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's 26-21 loss to the Broncos.
metadata.analysis: The veteran tight end was Bryce Young's favorite option on the afternoon, leading the Panthers in catches, targets and receiving yards, and Waller was on the other end of a 15-yard TD strike from the QB in the third quarter. It was Waller's most productive game since he returned from a brief retirement last season, and through eight games in 2026 he's put together a 23-299-4 line on 35 targets. He'll look to keep rolling in Week 10 against the Saints.

metadata.title: Darren Waller has Breakout Performance in Week 9
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller was a major factor in the offense during Sunday's Week 9 contest against the Denver Broncos. Heading into this game, Waller had two receptions for 61 yards over his last three games. The 34-year-old was able to have much more success on Sunday. He hauled in eight of his 10 targets for 90 yards and a touchdown in the loss. Both the receptions and yardage were season highs for Waller. It was odd to see Waller get double-digit targets after seeing a combined six over his previous three games. Fantasy managers shouldn't expect this kind of success to continue, but he'll hopefully remain a consistent option against the New Orleans Saints next week.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Seen on Sidelines at Tuesday's Practice
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller was spotted on the sidelines during Tuesday's practice, according to ESPN's Mike Kaye. The reason for his sideline activity has not been reported, leaving some uncertainty about his status ahead of Sunday's Week 9 matchup against the Denver Broncos. Carolina has previously given the 34-year-old scheduled veteran rest days, so his appearance on the sidelines does not necessarily indicate a new injury. Waller was not listed on the team's final Week 8 injury report and played against Green Bay last Thursday, catching one of two targets for 11 yards. He has recorded 15 receptions for 209 yards and three touchdowns across seven games, but has drawn just two targets in each of his past three appearances. Tommy Tremble and Mitchell Evans could see additional opportunities if Waller becomes unavailable, although his recent lack of involvement already limits his fantasy appeal.

metadata.title: Darren Waller - Makes one catch in Week 8
metadata.description: Waller corralled one of two targets for 11 yards during last Thursday's 27-19 loss at Green Bay.
metadata.analysis: Waller has been hit or miss from a fantasy perspective this season, with two touchdown grabs in Week 2 in Atlanta and a 50-yard TD catch in Week 7 against the Buccaneers serving as the notable performances. Otherwise, he has one 50-yard effort in his five other appearances, sitting on a 15-209-3 line on 25 targets on the season. Waller next takes aim at the tough Broncos defense this coming Sunday.

metadata.title: Darren Waller finishes with only one reception Thursday night
metadata.description: Darren Waller caught 1-of-2 targets for 11 yards in Thursday's 27-19 loss to the Packers.
metadata.analysis: Waller now has just two catches on a total of six targets over the last three weeks. Unlike in Week 7, when he scored on a 50-yard gain, the veteran TE was limited to just 11 yards in Week 8. Early on this season, it looked like Waller would be a significant contributor for the Panthers. That has now faded.

metadata.title: Darren Waller a Low-Level Fantasy Option in Tough Matchup
metadata.description: Carolina tight end Darren Waller has a very tough test awaiting in Week 8 against Green Bay on Thursday night. The Packers have been one of the toughest matchups for fantasy tight ends so far, and Waller himself hasn't delivered much, so the tight end is a low-level fantasy option for the coming week. Waller was a bit involved across the team's first four games, tallying at least two catches and 28 yards in each contest, but he's managed just one catch across the past two games combined. The reception was a 50-yard touchdown in Week 7 against Tampa Bay, so he still put up a solid fantasy score, but the bigger takeaway is his lack of involvement lately. He slots in 21st among tight ends in our RotoBaller Week 8 projections, showing he is a better option in deeper fantasy setups.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Remains an Extremely Risky Streaming Option
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller turned one of two targets into a 50-yard touchdown in Sunday's Week 7 loss to Tampa Bay, but the big play masked his limited role in a crowded tight end rotation. Waller logged just 45% of Carolina's offensive snaps, nearly identical to his 46% share in Week 6, and drew only four targets across those two games. The Panthers' tight end rotation leaves little room for optimism. Tommy Tremble played 68% of the snaps and scored twice against Philadelphia in Week 6, then saw his share fall to 48% against Tampa Bay while matching Waller with only two targets. Mitchell Evans also remains involved, logging snap shares of 54% and 50% over the past two weeks. With three tight ends competing for limited opportunities, Waller is a touchdown-or-bust desperation streamer, not a dependable fantasy option.

metadata.title: Darren Waller catches long TD in loss to Tampa
metadata.description: Darren Waller caught one of two targets for a 50-yard touchdown in the Panthers' 43-13 loss to the Buccaneers on Sunday,
metadata.analysis: If you have to only catch one ball, you might as well make it count. Waller rewarded those who started him with a long 50-yard score before going silent for the rest of the way. He's a risky start in fantasy despite some initial optimism for his role,

metadata.title: Darren Waller - Back in end zone during loss
metadata.description: Waller brought in one of two targets for a 50-yard touchdown in the Panthers' 43-13 loss to the Buccaneers on Sunday.
metadata.analysis: Waller's one catch not only netted Bryce Young his only passing touchdown of the day, but it also generated team-high receiving yardage. The veteran tight end's splash play naturally was a boon for his fantasy managers, but Waller has seen just four targets over the last two games after opening the season with multiple catches in each of the first four contests. Waller will take a 14-198-3 line into a Week 8 road matchup against the Packers on Thursday.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Snags Long Touchdown in Loss
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller was able to somewhat bounce back after posting a dud during last week's game. Waller ripped off a big score during Sunday's loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The veteran tight end scored a 50-yard touchdown, but that was his only catch of the game. It has not been an ideal season for Waller, who has only two games with 50 receiving yards or more heading into the Week 8 matchup against the Green Bay Packers. He's looking like a low-floor TE2 for that game.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Too Risky of a Bet in Week 7
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller needs to rebound in a big way, but it might not be enough for fantasy managers in Week 7 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. The veteran's fantasy value dipped after he posted goose eggs in Week 6, catching neither of his two targets against the Philadelphia Eagles. Waller was dealing with a toe injury before that game, but did not miss any time for injury-related reasons ahead of Sunday's game against Tampa Bay. The Buccaneers have struggled against the passing game, which could lead Bryce Young to vary his targets. However, Waller's diminished target share and poor Week 6 performance make him a risky bet, even as a deep-league streaming option.

metadata.title: Darren Waller blanked in Week 6
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller did not record a reception on two targets in a Week 6 win over Philadelphia.
metadata.analysis: Waller's two targets were his fewest since Week 1. He had 14 between Weeks 3 and 4 heading into a Week 5 bye, but tight end Tommy Tremble got involved with two touchdowns in Week 6. The Panthers' offense has been potent, but Tremble has been involved as well with 11 catches in the last three games.

metadata.title: Darren Waller - Quiet in Week 6 win
metadata.description: Waller failed to catch either of his two targets in Sunday's 25-14 win over the Eagles.
metadata.analysis: Waller dealt with a toe injury during the practice week and ended up playing behind both Tommy Tremble and Mitchell Evans in this one, as Tremble was the big producer in the box score, catching a pair of red-zone touchdowns. Waller is one of the many touchdown-or-bust fantasy options at the tight end position.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Looking to Remain Involved in Week 6 Game Versus Eagles
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller (toe) enters Sunday's Week 6 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles with 13 receptions for 148 yards (11.4 yards per reception) and two touchdowns. He will look to continue his solid production against the Eagles. Waller is dealing with a toe injury and was limited in practice on Wednesday and Thursday before being upgraded to a full participant on Friday. He will come into Sunday's game without an injury designation and is good to go. Waller faces a Philadelphia defense that allows 238.8 passing yards per game (26th in the NFL), but, according to Pro Football Reference, only gives up 4.9 fantasy points per game to tight end (eighth in the NFL). Waller has caught both of his touchdowns in the red zone this season. He is RotoBaller's No. 18 tight end for Week 6 (half-PPR).

metadata.title: Darren Waller - Good to go
metadata.description: Waller (toe) doesn't have an injury designation for Sunday's game at Philadelphia.
metadata.analysis: Waller should be fine to handle his usual role after upgrading to full practice participation Friday. He was limited Wednesday and Thursday, coming out of a Week 5 bye.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Carries No Injury Designation Into Week 6

He has caught 13 passes for 148 yards and two touchdowns through four games, with both scores coming against Atlanta in Week 2. His involvement in the passing game has increased recently, drawing eight targets against Cleveland in Week 3 and six against Detroit in Week 4 after receiving just five combined over the first two games. However, those 14 targets produced only eight catches for 87 yards without a touchdown. With Jalen Coker also cleared to play, Waller remains a touchdown-dependent TE2 option for fantasy managers in Week 6.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Remains Limited With Toe Injury
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller (toe) was limited in Thursday's practice, according to Joe Person, matching his estimated participation from Wednesday's walkthrough. Waller dealt with the same injury ahead of Carolina's Week 4 victory over Detroit but was able to play, catching three passes for 36 yards. The 34-year-old has recorded 13 receptions for 148 yards and two touchdowns on 19 targets through four games, with both scores coming against Atlanta in Week 2. His involvement has increased recently, drawing 14 targets over his last two appearances and turning those opportunities into eight catches for 87 yards. That usage offers some encouragement for fantasy managers, although Waller hasn't found the end zone since Week 2. Fellow tight end Tommy Tremble (ribs) has also been limited this week, leaving Carolina with some uncertainty at the position ahead of Sunday's matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles. Waller remains a potential streaming option in deeper leagues.

metadata.title: Darren Waller (toe) limited at practice Wednesday
metadata.description: Darren Waller (toe) was limited at practice on Wednesday.

metadata.title: Darren Waller - Tending to toe injury

Coming out of the team's Week 5 bye, though, both Waller and fellow TE Tommy Tremble (ribs, LP) are tending to injuries, leaving some question marks in the position group. Practices Thursday and Friday likely will determine if either of them enters the weekend with a designation for Sunday's game at Philadelphia.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Carries Limited Week 6 Streaming Appeal
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller returns from his Week 5 bye having drawn 14 targets over his last two games, but a difficult matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles makes him a risky fantasy option. Waller has caught 13 of 19 targets for 148 yards and two touchdowns through four games, with both scores coming against Atlanta in Week 2. His involvement increased against Cleveland and Detroit, although those 14 targets produced only eight receptions for 87 yards. Waller also played just 53% of Carolina's offensive snaps against the Lions, with Tommy Tremble and Mitchell Evans continuing to see substantial playing time. The Panthers could also welcome back Jalen Coker (quadriceps), who is reportedly on track to return after missing Week 4. Philadelphia has generally defended opposing tight ends well, adding another obstacle for a player whose fantasy production has been inconsistent outside his two-touchdown outing. Rostered in just 16% of leagues, Waller remains worth considering in 14-team formats, but his uncertain workload makes him a touchdown-dependent streaming option rather than a priority waiver addition.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Could Hit Waiver Wires with Panthers on Bye
metadata.description: In a Week 4 win played without one of the team's leading receivers, Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller caught only three passes for 36 yards. With Jalen Coker (quadriceps) sidelined by a quadriceps injury, the passing offense was funneled primarily through second-year receiver Tetairoa McMillan, who set or matched career highs across the board with 14 receptions on 16 targets, 192 yards, and two touchdowns. Still, despite a quiet outing, Waller remains a critical piece of one of the league's most improved offenses. Following a disappointing performance, and with the Panthers on a Week 5 bye, he is likely to hit waivers in a number of leagues, making the 34-year-old veteran an intriguing stash candidate for contending teams with adequate bench space. Unfortunately, the Panthers face an Eagles team in Week 6 that has been the most difficult tight end matchup through the first month of the season.

metadata.title: Darren Waller catches three passes Sunday night
metadata.description: Darren Waller hauled in 3-of-6 targets for 36 yards in Sunday's 32-26 win over the Lions.
metadata.analysis: In a game where Bryce Young cleared 300 yards passing and two of Carolina's top three wide receivers were out with injury, much more should have been expected from Waller. However, nearly half of Young's completions went to Tetairoa McMillan, who finished with almost 200 yards and a pair of touchdowns. That just did not leave much for Waller or any other Carolina route runner. The veteran remains a TD-dependent TE2.

metadata.title: Darren Waller Comes Up Short in Favorable Spot
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller had a favorable setup Sunday night and did very little with it. Waller caught three of six targets for 36 yards in the 32-26 win over Detroit, a disappointing result against a defense that had already allowed six touchdowns to tight ends through three games. The opportunity was there, too. Carolina played without Jalen Coker and Xavier Legette, while Bryce Young threw 41 passes for 329 yards. Waller still finished well behind Tetairoa McMillan, who dominated the passing game with 14 catches for 192 yards and two touchdowns. The veteran also played only 53% of the offensive snaps as Mitchell Evans and Tommy Tremble remained heavily involved. Waller has now gone two straight games without a touchdown after scoring twice in Week 2. With Carolina heading into its bye, his fantasy stock has cooled considerably.

metadata.title: Darren Waller - Held to three catches on SNF
metadata.description: Waller caught three of six targets for 36 yards in Sunday's 32-26 win over the Lions.
metadata.analysis: Waller finished second on the Panthers in targets and was one yard behind John Metchie for second on the team in receiving yards, but Tetairoa McMillan (14 catches for 192 yards and two TDs on 16 targets) was the clear No. 1 option in the passing game as the Panthers played without starting wide receiver Jalen Coker (quadriceps). The Lions had given up a league-high six touchdowns to tight ends entering play Sunday, but Waller was unable to add to that total. Waller and the Panthers will be on bye in Week 5 before facing the Eagles in Week 6.

metadata.title: Darren Waller a Priority Streaming Option in Week 4
metadata.description: The Carolina Panthers' receiver room is battling injuries, but tight end Darren Waller should see more targets in Week 4. Waller was dealing with a toe injury leading up to Week 4, but was off the injury list and a full practice participant on Friday. The veteran has hauled in 10 receptions on 13 targets for 112 yards this season, and his target share should spike in Week 4 since receiver Xavier Legette (knee) is out and Jalen Coker (quad) is questionable to play. Detroit has struggled to contain tight ends this season and is allowing a league-high 299.3 passing yards per game. Even if Coker plays, Waller is a priority streaming option against a struggling Detroit D.

metadata.title: Darren Waller a Premier Tight End Streamer Ahead of Week 4
metadata.description: Carolina Panthers tight end Darren Waller was heavily involved in his team's passing game in their Week 3 loss to the Cleveland Browns, recording five catches for 51 yards on eight targets. The 34-year-old has gotten off to a solid start to the season, hauling in 10 receptions for 112 yards and two touchdowns on 13 targets across three games. Waller's increased usage came after Panthers wide receiver Jalen Coker (quad) left the game with a quad strain. Coker reportedly avoided serious injury, but his status for Carolina's Week 4 matchup against the Detroit Lions is up in the air. Even if Coker plays, Waller could be in position for a big game in Week 4. The Lions' pass defense has really struggled to begin 2026 and has already given up six receiving touchdowns to tight ends this season.
